subject: Headcount deferral request + short-term succession plan for SRE IC
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Julie Park <julie@peopleops.redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Headcount deferral request + short-term succession plan for SRE IC

Team —

Quick context: Senior SRE (IC-3) on Platform left effective 2026-09-01; role was approved in Q2 plan. Recruiting is paused per the companywide hiring freeze, but the on-call and reliability gap is material for the infra stack that backs Redwood Dedicated.

As a compromise between strict freeze adherence and operational risk, I propose the following path and request a narrow, time-boxed exception:

1) Deferral window: delay backfill for up to 6 months rather than immediate hire. During that period we implement the short-term succession plan below.
2) Succession plan (temporary coverage):
  - Promote (scope elevation) senior IC: shift L2 SRE (internal: Priya substitution) to cover on-call rotation with 15% temporary compensation adjustment + mentorship from surviving senior SRE.
  - Contract coverage: engage one senior contractor via TalentBridge for critical paging w/ 3-month retainer + 30-day notice (contract-to-hire optional).
  - Reduce noncritical change windows to minimize incident surface area.

I attach org_chart_Q3.pdf and a short succession_notes.txt with role split and escalation matrix. This approach preserves institutional knowledge, reduces immediate spend vs a full-time hire, and keeps the role on plan for Q1 when recruiting reopens.

Requesting approvals on 3 items:
- Limited hiring freeze exception for a short-term contractor (cost center: Infra Ops 4201)
- Temporary comp uplift for L2 SRE (one headcount re-scope, no additional FTE)
- Confirmation that the role remains in the org plan to fund full backfill after deferral

Please reply with green/red and any objections. I need a decision by tomorrow EOD so we can secure contractor availability.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: org_chart_Q3.pdf (org chart), succession_notes.txt (succession split and on-call matrix)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Julie Park <julie@peopleops.redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Headcount deferral request + short-term succession plan for SRE IC

Mina — thanks for the clear plan. I support a narrow exception but want to flag two operational risks and a suggestion: 

- On-call fatigue: pulling the L2 into a heavier on-call load will increase MTTR risk if they are juggling too many projects. Keep rotations tight (1 week max).
- SLA exposure for Dedicated customers: we need to document rollback and playbooks for the next 12 months.

Suggestion: Approve a 3-month contractor retainer first (cost estimate ~ $45k) and re-evaluate at 90 days. If recruiting opens earlier, we expedite. That minimizes long-term spend while covering immediate risk.

I've attached a short role scorecard (sre_role_scorecard.xlsx) with must-have vs nice-to-have skills — will help when we brief Procurement.

Vivek
VP, Engineering Operations

Agree with Vivek on a shorter exception window. Recruiting update (for visibility): we have two screened internal referrals who match the basic SRE checklist but neither has the depth for Dedicated-level incidents. We also have one offer accepted for an infra engineering role that could be re-skilled, but that would add ~6 weeks ramp.

If PeopleOps can sign off on a 3-month contractor with contract-to-hire terms, I think we balance risk and compliance. I do not recommend pulling any L3 from feature teams.

Quick ask: can we tie the approval to a weekly incident review for the 3 months so leadership can track operational risk? I can run that with platform SREs.

Hi Mina / team —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the attachments. PeopleOps can provisionally approve a time-boxed exception under the following conditions: 

1) Limited exception: approve a 3-month contractor retainer (TalentBridge) with a mandatory review at day-60 to determine continuation.
2) No permanent FTE commitment during the 3-month window; the role remains in the org plan and will be funded when hiring re-opens.
3) Documented mitigation: weekly incident review (Aditya to run) and updated runbooks uploaded to the Shared Drive (link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/abc123-org-chart).
4) Budget signoff: Finance needs to approve the contractor cost center (Infra Ops 4201). Please route to procurement@redwood.com with the attached scorecard and cost estimate.
5) Exec notification: VP of Eng (Vivek) to confirm SLA risk tolerance in writing; I have cc'd Laura for awareness and final note.

If you can confirm acceptance of the above, PeopleOps will spin up the contractor PO and the temporary comp uplift process for the L2 (if invoked). I will queue this for VP signoff — please reply with a single-line approval so I can put it on the exec queue.

Julie Park
